To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the small manufacturing firms' hazard rates are positively related to the firms' debt ratios, the ratio of working capital to fixed assets, the ratio of the value of the firm to the value of the fixed assets and to the ratio of the firm's age to the average age of all the firms in the same industry; they are negatively related to the ratio of fixed assets to working capital, the ratio of investment to the market value of the firm, the ratio of fixed capital to the value of fixed assets
the very small manufacturing enterprises' survival prospects are determined by their financing and investment policies, by their market strategies, and by their economic environment.

the small manufacturing enterprise survival rates are negatively associated with the use of the overdrafts and other short-term loans to finance the fixed investment, with the fixed investment financed with the retained earnings, with the fixed asset replacement rate and with the use of subcontracting.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the survival prospects of the very small enterprises of the traditional manufacturing sectors in Brazil and it is the first to identify determinants of the hazard rates of the incumbent very small manufacturing enterprises.

the small manufacturing firms' hazard rate is a function of their financing, working capital, production technology policies, matching of investment and debt financing maturities and market strategies, of the characteristics of the entrepreneurs, of the riskiness of the businesses and of the economic climate.

the very small enterprises of the traditional manufacturing sectors in Brazil are not doomed to fail, as is often claimed, but that the small business managers' decisions are of crucial relevance for the survival of the small enterprises.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small firms' survival is a function of the entrepreneur's ability in making good decisions.
the very small manufacturing firms' survival prospects depend on a wide array of variables and that the survival of the very small manufacturing enterprises is a complex matter.

the small businesses' survival prospects seem to depend on the same factors that determine the survival of the large firms, but the small enterprises' survival prospects are also dependent on the characteristics of the entrepreneurs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the small firms' survival is a complex process, and that the traditional determinants, such as the age and size of the business, the entrepreneur's education and the industry of operation, are not the most important ones.
the very small firms are a special case of the small business.
small business survival is a matter of business strategy and that the small business literature should pay more attention to the management of the small businesses.
